::: {.lead}
Today you build the small database of the Sunrise shop. Each experiment
has two parts. **Part A** is in Microsoft Access on the lab computer.
**Part B** is on a simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its
QR code; on the screen, click its link. After each step, write your result
in its box. At the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Microsoft Access (Windows). There is
  no start file: you type three short records.
- **No Access?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Access is
  only on Windows computers.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

## Experiment 1 · A table: fields and data types

**The idea:** a **database** keeps data in **tables**. A table has
**fields** (the columns, such as Name) and **records** (the rows: one
customer). Each field has a **data type**: Short Text (names, phone
numbers), Number (to count), Currency (money), Date/Time, Yes/No.

**Aim:** make a table with the right data types, and type its records.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Access)**
:::

1. Open Access. Click **Blank database**, name it `shop` and click
   **Create**. Click **View › Design View**, and save the table as
   `Customers`. Type the fields: `CustomerID` (AutoNumber), `Name` (Short
   Text), `City` (Short Text).

   {{< record "Data type of Name: … ; of CustomerID: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Name: Short Text** (a name is text). **CustomerID: AutoNumber**:
   Access gives every new record the next number by itself.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which data type is right for the field Name?

   - [x] Short Text

     Why: A name is text.

   - [ ] Number

     Why: You never add or count names.

   - [ ] Yes/No

     Why: A name is not yes or no.
   :::

2. Click **View › Datasheet View**. Type three records: Huda, Amman · Omar,
   Zarqa · Lina, Amman. (Access writes the CustomerID.)

   {{< record "The table has … records and … fields" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **3 records** (Huda, Omar, Lina) and **3 fields** (CustomerID, Name,
   City). A record is a row; a field is a column.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="3" unit="records" hint="One row for each customer."}
   Huda, Omar and Lina are in the Customers table. How many records does it
   have?

   Why: One record (row) for each customer: 3 records.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/field-lab.html" poster="sims/field-lab.png" title="Field Lab: the right data type" >}}

3. In **Field Lab**, choose the data type of the six fields. Which type is
   right for Price, and which for InStock?

   {{< record "Price: … ; InStock: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Price: Currency** (money). **InStock: Yes/No** (only two answers).
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which data type? Sort the fields.

   Currency
   :   Price (2.00 JD)

       Why: Money is Currency.

   Yes/No
   :   InStock (Yes or No)

       Why: Only two answers.

   Short Text
   :   Phone (079 000 0001)

       Why: You never add phone numbers, and the 0 at the start must stay.

   Date/Time
   :   OrderDate (03/11/2026)

       Why: A date.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · The primary key and a relationship

**The idea:** the **primary key** is the field with a different value in
every record (CustomerID); a name or a city can repeat. A second table,
**Orders**, has the field CustomerID too. A **relationship** joins the two
tables with this field: **one** customer has **many** orders
(one-to-many).

**Aim:** find the primary key, and join two tables.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Access)**
:::

1. Open the Customers table in **Design View**. Look for the small key
   next to a field.

   {{< record "The primary key of Customers is" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **CustomerID**: it has a different value in every record. Two customers
   can have the same name or city.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Why is Name not a good primary key?

   - [x] Two customers can have the same name.

     Why: A primary key must be different in every record.

   - [ ] A name is too long.

     Why: Length does not matter; a key must not repeat.

   - [ ] Names are text.

     Why: Text keys are possible, but names repeat.
   :::

2. Make a table `Orders`: `OrderID` (AutoNumber), `CustomerID` (Number),
   `Item` (Short Text), `Total` (Currency). Click **Database Tools ›
   Relationships**, add both tables, and drag **CustomerID** from Customers
   onto CustomerID in Orders. Tick **Enforce Referential Integrity** and
   click **Create**.

   {{< record "The line shows … next to Customers and … next to Orders" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **1** next to Customers and **∞** (many) next to Orders: one customer
   has many orders.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   What does the line 1 — ∞ between Customers and Orders mean?

   - [x] One customer can have many orders.

     Why: 1 is next to Customers, ∞ (many) next to Orders.

   - [ ] One order can have many customers.

     Why: Each order belongs to one customer.

   - [ ] The tables have the same records.

     Why: They share only the field CustomerID.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/key-lab.html" poster="sims/key-lab.png" title="Key Lab: the primary key and the relationship" >}}

3. In **Key Lab**, do Tasks 1 to 4. In Task 3, which field joins Orders to
   Customers?

   {{< record "Task 3: the field" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **CustomerID**: the same field is in both tables.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   In Task 3, which field joins Orders to Customers?

   - [x] CustomerID

     Why: The same field is in both tables.

   - [ ] OrderID

     Why: OrderID is only in the Orders table.

   - [ ] Item

     Why: Item is only in the Orders table.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · A query: a criterion and a sort

**The idea:** a **query** asks a table a question. It shows only the
fields and the records that you ask for. A **criterion** chooses the
records (City = Amman, Price > 5); a **sort** puts them in order
(ascending: A to Z, small to big). **Create › Query Design**, then **Run**.

**Aim:** show only the records that you need, in order.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Access)**
:::

1. Click **Create › Query Design** and add the Customers table. Double-click
   **Name** and **City**. In the **Criteria** row under City, type `Amman`.
   Click **Run** (the red !).

   {{< record "The query shows … records: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **2 records: Huda and Lina** (both in Amman). Omar (Zarqa) is not
   shown, but he is still in the table.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="2" unit="records" hint="Count the customers in Amman."}
   Huda (Amman), Omar (Zarqa), Lina (Amman). How many records does the
   query City = Amman show?

   Why: Only Huda and Lina live in Amman.
   :::

2. Go back to **Design View**. In the **Sort** row under Name, choose
   **Ascending**, and Run again. Save the query as `AmmanCustomers`.

   {{< record "The first name now is" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Huda**: ascending sorts the names from A to Z (H comes before L).
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The query shows Lina and Huda. After the sort Name, Ascending, which
   name is first?

   - [x] Huda

     Why: Ascending is A to Z, and H comes before L.

   - [ ] Lina

     Why: Lina is first only with Descending.

   - [ ] Omar

     Why: Omar is not in the query: he lives in Zarqa.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/query-lab.html" poster="sims/query-lab.png" title="Query Lab: ask the table a question" >}}

3. In **Query Lab**, do Tasks 1 to 3. Task 2: how many products cost more
   than 5 JD?

   {{< record "Task 2: … records" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **2 records**: the Bag (12 JD) and the Lunch box (6 JD).
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="2" unit="records" hint="Look at the Price column: which prices are above 5?"}
   The Products table: Notebook 2, Pen 0.50, Bag 12, Water 0.50, Juice 1,
   Folder 1.50, Lunch box 6, Coffee 1 (JD). How many records does the
   criterion Price > 5 show?

   Why: Only the Bag (12) and the Lunch box (6) cost more than 5 JD.
   :::
